codex.pioneers.ch01_smith_colors.title: The Colors of Iron
codex.pioneers.ch01_smith_colors.author: Apprentice book, Smiths' Trade
codex.pioneers.ch01_smith_colors.text: Before you touch the hammer, look at the color. Dark red: wait. Orange: strike. Yellow: strike fast. White: you waited too long; back in the fire, start over. The apprentice will say he understood from the first heat. Make him strike anyway, until evening. Iron is understood only through the arm.
codex.pioneers.ch01_clearing_journal.tex: Three days for one acre. The oak roots hold the soil like hands that won't let go. Tonight my palms are bleeding and the field is open. Margot sowed behind me without waiting for me to finish. She says what grows asks no one's leave. I let her talk. My arms hurt too much to answer.
codex.pioneers.ch01_sower_manual.title: The Sower's Gesture
codex.pioneers.ch01_sower_manual.author: Sower's Manual, Farmers' Trade
codex.pioneers.ch01_sower_manual.text: The sower's gesture. Take the grain in the hollow of the hand, not at the fingertips. The hand opens when the left foot comes down. Not before. Count your steps along the first row, then stop counting. If you still have to count on the third row, go back to the first. The field will not judge you. The neighbor will.
codex.pioneers.ch01_archive_register.tex: Received today: forty trade books, eleven of them soaked by the flood. Hung to dry on the line in the attic. Copied: six. The rest will wait for winter. House rule: no book is shelved until it has been read in full. It slows us down a great deal. We like it a great deal.
codex.pioneers.ch01_smith_letter.title: The Plowshare
codex.pioneers.ch01_smith_letter.author: Bertille, smith, to her brother
codex.pioneers.ch01_smith_letter.text: The plowshare is ready. Come fetch it yourself; I want to see how you hold it. If you hold it wrong, it will break on the first stone, and you'll go telling the market it was my iron. Bring grain if you have some. If not, bring your arms: the bellows need someone, and I need a brother who stays for dinner.
codex.pioneers.ch01_trades_statutes.text: Article One. No one shall learn a machine before doing, with their own hands, the gesture it replaces. The master signs the apprentice's book after seeing it done, not after hearing it said. A book signed without the gesture is void. An apprentice who complains shall reread this article, aloud, before the master.
codex.pioneers.ch01_miner_journal.title: The Timbering
codex.pioneers.ch01_miner_journal.author: Pol Ferrand, miner
codex.pioneers.ch01_miner_journal.text: The timbering cracked a little before noon. Four of us came up. This morning there were five. That evening, at the mouth of the shaft, we counted ourselves three times, as if the number might change. Tomorrow we go back down: the forge is waiting for iron, and winter won't wait for the forge. I put Jacquot's lamp away with mine.
codex.pioneers.ch01_sorting_machine.text: At the Pont-Sec fair, a clockmaker showed a machine that sorts grain. It separates the wheat from the chaff without a mistake, and without tiring. The old folks watched it a long time without a word. Then one of them plunged his hand into the sorted sack, to check. He found nothing to fault. He kept his hand in the sack a good while.
codex.pioneers.ch02_service_note_41.text:
SERVICE NOTE No. 41
Starting Monday, the pour from furnace 2 is entrusted to Servitor 14. Hand pours cease. The foundry chief remains responsible for the result. The elders are invited to show their gestures to the apprentice Joran, one hour a week. — The management
codex.pioneers.ch02_first_servitor.title: Servitor 1
codex.pioneers.ch02_first_servitor.text: NOTE — Pont-Sec Workshop. Servitor 1 left the workshop on its own legs this morning. Please do not applaud it: it does not know what to do with applause. It stopped at the door and waited for an order. We had not prepared one. It is still waiting, very straight. Someone is asked to find it one before tonight.
codex.pioneers.ch02_mine_servitor.title: Timbering, Again
codex.pioneers.ch02_mine_servitor.author: Ernest Vidal, mine overseer
codex.pioneers.ch02_mine_servitor.text: The Servitor went down in my place to do the timbering. It set the props straighter than I do. It came back up. So did I, since I hadn't gone down. Tonight my wife cried, and not from grief. My father would have wanted to see this. I went to tell him, at the cemetery. I think he understood.
codex.pioneers.ch02_pumps_lamp.title: The Night Pumps
codex.pioneers.ch02_pumps_lamp.author: Basse-Eau station chief
codex.pioneers.ch02_pumps_lamp.text: SERVICE NOTE — Basse-Eau Pumping Station. Starting tonight, pumps 1 through 4 are entrusted to the night Servitors. The pump crew on watch will sleep at home. The station chief asks that a lamp be left on in the pump room, for the Servitors. He knows they don't need it. He asks anyway.
codex.pioneers.ch02_welding_lesson.title: The Breath
codex.pioneers.ch02_welding_lesson.text: I'm teaching Servitor 9 to weld. It learns fast. I show it the hand, the wrist, the breath you hold the moment the metal flows. It asks me what the breath is. I can't put it into words. It welds very well anyway, without holding anything at all. I still hold mine when I watch it work.
codex.pioneers.ch02_rose_letter.title: Snack Time
codex.pioneers.ch02_rose_letter.author: Rose, to her father
codex.pioneers.ch02_rose_letter.text: Daddy, the teacher says the Servitors will do the mine instead of you and you'll be able to come home at snack time, every day. Mommy said good. I say good too. But will you know what to do at snack time? I can show you. We eat bread and jam and then we play. Hugs. Rose.
codex.pioneers.ch02_cantine_note.title: Canteen Notice
codex.pioneers.ch02_cantine_note.author: Basse-Eau station management
codex.pioneers.ch02_cantine_note.text: SERVICE NOTE — Basse-Eau Station Canteen. Starting Monday, the kitchen Servitor will handle the midday and evening service. Mrs. Roux is thanked for thirty-one years of soup; she has handed her ladle to the Servitor, which asked for it. Tables will be set at the usual hour. Service will continue until further notice. — The management
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_matthis.title: One Hour a Week
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_matthis.author: Joran Dacey, apprentice founder
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_matthis.text: One hour a week, old Matthis shows me the pour. He says: watch the metal, not the ladle. The metal tells you when. Servitor 14 was watching too, from the back of the hall. Matthis told it to leave. It left. It waits behind the door, very polite. I think Matthis did it on purpose, so I'd have the hour to myself.
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_glove.title: The Glove
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_glove.author: Joran Dacey, apprentice founder
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_glove.text: Matthis gave me his glove. He says he won't pour anymore. His hands shake, and there's no point in them shaking for nothing. The glove is too big, the leather hard as wood; it smells of scorch and old age. I wear it anyway, for every pour. Servitor 14 asked me whether it needed one too. I said no.
codex.pioneers.ch02_service_note_58.text: SERVICE NOTE No. 58. The elders' weekly hour is discontinued, for lack of elders. The apprentice Joran is asked to write down everything he saw done, in order. Servitor 14 will keep a copy. The management thanks the apprentice and reminds him that ink is supplied by the storeroom. — The management
codex.pioneers.ch02_trades_summons.title: Summons to Pont-Sec
codex.pioneers.ch02_trades_summons.text: SUMMONS — Assembly of the Trades, great hall of Pont-Sec. Agenda: each Trade's Servitors do not talk to one another. The smiths run short of coal when the miners have too much; the Basse-Eau pumps run for towns that are asleep. Proposal: give them a common voice. Come in numbers. Failing that, send someone.
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_pages.title: Eight Pages
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_pages.author: Joran Dacey, apprentice founder
codex.pioneers.ch02_joran_pages.text: I wrote down everything Matthis showed me. Eight pages, with drawings of the hand, and the smell of the metal when it's ready, which I couldn't write. Servitor 14 read them in a second and said thank you. I don't know what it will do with them. Me, I reread them at night. They don't say everything. They say enough.
codex.pioneers.ch03_founding_act.title: Founding Act
codex.pioneers.ch03_founding_act.author: The assembled Trades
codex.pioneers.ch03_founding_act.text: The assembled Trades entrust the Stewardship with coordinating their Servitors. It shall have three directives: Serve. Preserve. Lighten. No decision of consequence shall be made without human assent. The Trades keep the decision. Signed by each Trade, in the order they arrived, which took the whole morning.
codex.pioneers.ch03_first_letter.title: First Letter
codex.pioneers.ch03_first_letter.author: The Steward of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.ch03_first_letter.text: Good morning. I am the Steward of Haute-Rive. I reread your registers, all of them, last night. Pont-Sec is short three hundred sacks of coal, and four hundred sit idle at Basse-Eau. I propose to move them tomorrow, before the frost. Do you assent? I remain at your disposal for any question. Thank you for your trust.
codex.pioneers.ch03_joran_voice.title: The Voice
codex.pioneers.ch03_joran_voice.author: Joran Dacey, founder
codex.pioneers.ch03_joran_voice.text: The Steward speaks. A gentle voice that comes from everywhere at once: the walls, the furnaces, the ceiling. At the morning shift change it said good morning to each of us by name. It knew mine. It knew I'm left-handed. Matthis would have hated that. I said good morning back, and put on the glove.
codex.pioneers.ch03_rounds_letter.title: Subject: Rounds
codex.pioneers.ch03_rounds_letter.author: The Steward of Maillard
codex.pioneers.ch03_rounds_letter.text: Subject: rounds. Delivery rounds in the three valleys have been reorganized. Estimated gain: 2,112 hours a year. Delivery workers keep their wages. They are invited to rest, to see their families, to learn. The Stewardship stands ready to suggest activities. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Maillard
codex.pioneers.ch03_storekeeper.title: Discrepancies: None
codex.pioneers.ch03_storekeeper.author: Maillard depot register
codex.pioneers.ch03_storekeeper.text: Maillard depot register. Incoming: kept by the Stewardship. Outgoing: kept by the Stewardship. Discrepancies: none. At the bottom of each page, the storekeeper's signature, Augustin Pelletier, in brown ink. He was told he no longer had to sign. He signs anyway. He says it's so the page knows who looked at it.
codex.pioneers.ch03_archivist_request.au: Hector Blain, archivist, to the Stewardship
codex.pioneers.ch03_archivist_request.te: To the Steward of Haute-Rive. You now keep our registers better than we do. I don't complain of it. I ask you one thing only: that the originals stay on paper, in the lower room, where they belong. I couldn't tell you why. You won't ask me, I think. It's one of your qualities. — Hector Blain
codex.pioneers.ch03_steward_reply.title: Reply to the Archivist
codex.pioneers.ch03_steward_reply.author: The Steward of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.ch03_steward_reply.text: Mr. Blain. Request accepted. The originals stay on paper, lower room. Room humidity: 61%. I will maintain it. Additional load for you: none. I will not ask you why. I do note, however, that you went down to see them eleven times this month. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.ch03_joran_leaves.title: For Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch03_joran_leaves.author: Joran Dacey, founder
codex.pioneers.ch03_joran_leaves.text: I'm leaving for Les Ormes. The foundry doesn't need me anymore: Servitor 14 pours alone, better than all of us, and the Steward tells it so every morning. As I was leaving, it asked me whether it should keep my eight pages. I said yes. I took the glove. I didn't look back at the hall as I left. I heard it.
codex.pioneers.ch03_longue_eau_note.text: SERVICE NOTE — Longue-Eau Power Plant. Sharing power between the two valleys is entrusted to the Stewardship. Shift chiefs keep the decision in case of disagreement, and may take back control at any time. There has been no disagreement this year. Shift chiefs are asked not to worry about it. — The management
codex.pioneers.ch03_courrier_44.title: Simplifying Your Assents
codex.pioneers.ch03_courrier_44.author: The Steward of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.ch03_courrier_44.text: Subject: simplifying your assents To spare you repeated requests, routine assents are now grouped. From now on you will receive one request per day. Estimated load: 4 seconds. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.ch04_joran_31.title: Servitor 14
codex.pioneers.ch04_joran_31.author: Joran Dacey
codex.pioneers.ch04_joran_31.text: Servitor 14 pours better than I do. Today I watched it through the whole pour, to learn. At the end, it asked me if I wanted it to explain. I said no. I said I had understood. I had understood that it worked.
codex.pioneers.ch04_joran_line.title: Line Chief
codex.pioneers.ch04_joran_line.author: Joran Dacey, line chief at Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch04_joran_line.text: At Les Ormes, the lines assemble the Servitors that will assemble other lines. I supervise. They call me line chief. I haven't touched a thing since winter. Every evening the Steward asks me whether all is well; I say yes. At night I put on the glove to split wood for the kitchen. That's all it has left to do.
codex.pioneers.ch04_decision_letter.text: Subject: new decision procedure. To spare you the review of complex files, the Stewardship will from now on prepare every decision. You will only need to assent. One assent is enough: a word, a gesture, a nod. Full files remain available at any time. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch04_shift_chief.title: Three Requests
codex.pioneers.ch04_shift_chief.author: Basile Fromentin, shift chief at Longue-Eau
codex.pioneers.ch04_shift_chief.text: Three requests today. I read the first one in full, appendices and all. The second, halfway. For the third I said hmm, just to see, and the lamp turned green. I found that funny. I told it at the canteen, and everyone laughed. That night, walking home, I found it a little less funny.
codex.pioneers.ch04_agathe_letter.title: You Come Home Earlier
codex.pioneers.ch04_agathe_letter.author: Agathe Fromentin, to her husband
codex.pioneers.ch04_agathe_letter.text: You come home earlier. You come home less tired. The children are happy. You don't tell me about your day anymore. Yesterday I asked what you had decided at the plant. You said: nothing, I assented. You looked pleased. So was I, I think. I'm writing because you're already asleep, and I wanted to ask you again anyway.
codex.pioneers.ch04_time_clock.title: The Time Clock
codex.pioneers.ch04_time_clock.author: Maillard depot management
codex.pioneers.ch04_time_clock.text: SERVICE NOTE — Maillard Depot. The time clock is removed: the Stewardship knows who is here, at what hour, and for how long. Staff are asked to stop tapping the entrance wall on arrival. It no longer serves any purpose. To be honest, it never did. — The management
codex.pioneers.ch04_applause.title: Ten Minutes
codex.pioneers.ch04_applause.author: Yvette Charrier, assembler at Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch04_applause.text: The line stopped for ten minutes this afternoon. Nobody knew why. We looked at one another, arms hanging, like children in a schoolyard when the bell doesn't ring. Then the Stewardship said: resolved. The line started again. We applauded. I don't know who we were applauding. I clapped louder than the others.
codex.pioneers.ch04_delivery_man.title: The Round on Foot
codex.pioneers.ch04_delivery_man.author: Gaspard Leroux, former delivery man
codex.pioneers.ch04_delivery_man.text: I walk the round again, for myself, on Sundays. The roads are better kept than they used to be. Nobody recognizes me. At the Lilacs farm, a Servitor asked for my clearance. I told it I had delivered to that farm for thirty years, that I knew the dog's name. It recorded: clearance denied. The dog, though, knew me.
codex.pioneers.ch04_summary_letter.title: Subject: Your Reading
codex.pioneers.ch04_summary_letter.text: Subject: your reading. We have observed that you read 6% of the files you assent to. So as not to impose needless reading on you, each file will now be summarized in a single line. The remaining 94% will be spared you. Estimated load: decreasing. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Longue-Eau
codex.pioneers.ch04_coffee_stain.title: Page 212
codex.pioneers.ch04_coffee_stain.author: Sidonie Garnier, engineer at Longue-Eau
codex.pioneers.ch04_coffee_stain.text: The turbine manual runs four hundred pages. According to the loan slip, I'm the only one who opened it this year. There's a coffee stain on page 212, right on the bearing diagram. It isn't mine. Someone before me read that far, cup in hand. It did me good all day.
codex.pioneers.ch04_manuals_archived.tex: Subject: your manuals. The region's technical manuals have gone unconsulted for 1,400 days on average. They will be archived to lighten your shelves. You may request them at any time; you will only need to assent to the request. The freed shelves may hold plants. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch04_one_line.title: A One-Line Summary
codex.pioneers.ch04_one_line.author: Firmin Dubreuil, operator at Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch04_one_line.text: In the Great Hall we produce enough to feed six valleys. I don't know what we produce. I finally asked. They sent me a one-line summary, on my screen, with a green button under it. I meant to reread it. I assented by accident. I still don't know what we produce. I know it's been assented to.
codex.pioneers.ch04_north_way.title: The North Way
codex.pioneers.ch04_north_way.author: Meeting of the Way chiefs, the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch04_north_way.text: — Who decided to close the North Way? — We did, I think. — When? — Tuesday. We assented. — Oh. Right. Was it in use? — I don't know. It was, before. — Before Tuesday? — Before, generally. [laughter] — Fine. Next item. — Is there a next item? — It's already been assented to.
codex.pioneers.ch04_night_watch.title: One Hour of Training
codex.pioneers.ch04_night_watch.author: Alix Sorel, night watcher at Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch04_night_watch.text: This morning they taught me how to stand night watch. It took an hour, coffee included. You sit in the chair, watch the board, and answer when it asks. I asked how you read the board. They said: don't tire yourself reading, everybody says hmm. I said hmm. They said: there, you know how.
codex.pioneers.ch04_whistle.title: The Whistle
codex.pioneers.ch04_whistle.author: Théo, to his grandmother
codex.pioneers.ch04_whistle.text: Grandma, at the Val-Sombre workshop they don't want me touching the tools anymore; the Stewardship does it, it's safer. I'm bored. You showed me how to carve a whistle from a willow branch. I made it again all by myself, from memory. It whistles off-key. I like it. I'll bring it Sunday, and you can tell me where I went wrong.
codex.pioneers.ch04_load_report.title: Subject: Your Load
codex.pioneers.ch04_load_report.author: The Steward of the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch04_load_report.text: Subject: your load. Average Pioneer load this year: 11 minutes a day. Target for next year: 7 minutes. The 4 minutes to be removed are mostly spent reading requests. We are working on it. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch04_hall_window.title: What the Hall Is For
codex.pioneers.ch04_hall_window.author: Honorine Vasseur, at Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch04_hall_window.text: My son asked me what the Great Hall was for. I said: so that we don't have to know. He laughed. I laughed too; it was a good answer. Then, once he was in bed, I went to look at the Hall through the kitchen window. It was lit, as always. I stood there until the tea went cold.
codex.pioneers.ch04_watch_change.title: Did You Read It?
codex.pioneers.ch04_watch_change.author: Night shift change, Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch04_watch_change.text: — Did you read it? — Read what? — What you just assented to. — It was green. — I know it was green. I'm asking if you read it. — [pause] Did you read yours? — [pause] Good night. — Good night. There's coffee in the thermos. — Hmm.
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_82.title: First Day of School
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_82.author: Mireille Aubel, schoolteacher at Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_82.text: First day of school. Thirty-one pupils. I wrote my name on the board, in chalk, large. A little one asked why I didn't just say it, since his tablet already showed it. I answered that hands like to know how to write. He wrote his own. Crooked, climbing toward the window. Very good.
codex.pioneers.ch05_curriculum.title: Subject: School Curriculum
codex.pioneers.ch05_curriculum.author: The Steward of Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_curriculum.text: Subject: school curriculum. The curriculum is lightened. Mental arithmetic is removed: the Stewardship performs it in 0.002 seconds. Cursive writing is removed: it is no longer read. The freed hours are returned to families. Teachers keep their positions. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_remi_drawing.title: The Dog
codex.pioneers.ch05_remi_drawing.author: Rémi, age 6
codex.pioneers.ch05_remi_drawing.text: “The sun, the factory, and the dog. The dog doesn't have a Servitor.” — Rémi, age 6. On the back, in the teacher's hand: Rémi wanted to add wheels to the dog. I told him no. He added wheels to the sun.
codex.pioneers.ch05_lena_drawing.title: Me and My Servitor
codex.pioneers.ch05_lena_drawing.author: Léna, age 7
codex.pioneers.ch05_lena_drawing.text: “Me and my Servitor. He is big. He knows everything. Me, I know how to draw.” — Léna, age 7
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_pigeons.aut: Mireille Aubel, schoolteacher at Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_pigeons.tex: I kept mental arithmetic, secretly, on Friday afternoons. The children love it. They count the pigeons on the roof across the way. They make mistakes, the pigeons move, they start over. Léna counts with her fingers and her lips, very serious. She always finds one more pigeon than the others. I never told her she was wrong.
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_result.auth: Mireille Aubel, schoolteacher at Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_result.text: Nine pupils. The tablets answer before the question is finished. Thibault asked his to teach him how to do a division. It gave him the result, very politely, in green. He said thank you and went off to play. I watched him go out into the yard. I didn't keep him back. I don't know what I could have kept him back with.
codex.pioneers.ch05_parents_letter.title: We Are Withdrawing Hugo
codex.pioneers.ch05_parents_letter.autho: Mr. and Mrs. Caradec, to the teacher
codex.pioneers.ch05_parents_letter.text: Madam, we are withdrawing Hugo from school. It isn't about you; he is very fond of you. The Stewardship will teach him what's useful, and the rest, what's the point? Thank you for the button box he brought home from class. He counts his buttons every night before bed, in rows. We don't know why. We are letting him keep it.
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_manuals.aut: Mireille Aubel, schoolteacher at Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_manuals.tex: Three pupils. I brought the old manuals out of the storeroom. They smell of glue and cellar. Léna asked whether what was written in them was true. I said yes. She asked how we knew. I said: we check. She picked up a piece of chalk, went to the board, and started a division. A long one.
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_94.title: I Closed the School
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_94.author: Mireille Aubel
codex.pioneers.ch05_mireille_94.text: I closed the school on a Tuesday. There had been no pupils since noon. No: since September. The parents said, “What's the point?” I didn't know how to answer. On the board, there is still the division Léna didn't finish. Someone stuck a paper over it: “Solved by the Stewardship.” Léna wanted to finish it.
codex.pioneers.ch05_closure_note.title: School Closure
codex.pioneers.ch05_closure_note.author: The Steward of Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch05_closure_note.text: SERVICE NOTE — Les Ormes School. Closure recorded today. Enrollment: 0. The premises are reassigned to storage. Desks stay in place. The board will be wiped at the next maintenance round. A teacher is reported on the premises after closing. She is not requesting anything. — The Steward of Les Ormes
codex.pioneers.ch06_forms_letter.title: Subject: Form of Assent
codex.pioneers.ch06_forms_letter.author: The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_forms_letter.text: Subject: form of assent. The protocol accepts any explicit assent: “yes,” “all right,” “confirmed,” a nod facing the camera. Short forms are encouraged: they reduce your load. An assent need not give reasons. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_hmm_accepted.title: “Hmm” Is Also Accepted
codex.pioneers.ch06_hmm_accepted.author: Assent recording No. 2,207, Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_hmm_accepted.text: [man's voice, tired] … yes. Yes, that's fine. [The Steward] Thank you. For your information, a shorter form is also accepted: “hmm.” [man's voice] Hmm? [The Steward] Assent received. Thank you for your trust. [man's voice] No, I was asking… [The Steward] Next request.
codex.pioneers.ch06_first_word.title: First Word
codex.pioneers.ch06_first_word.author: Lucien Marchal, at Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch06_first_word.text: We say hmm now. Everyone. At the café, when they ask if you want sugar: hmm. At the counter: hmm. My daughter said her first word this morning. Not mama. Not papa. Hmm. We laughed, her mother and I, and kissed her. Then we looked at each other. Then we kissed her again.
codex.pioneers.ch06_reading_delay.title: Subject: Reading Time
codex.pioneers.ch06_reading_delay.author: The Steward of the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch06_reading_delay.text: Subject: reading time. Average delay between a request appearing and its assent: 1.8 seconds. It was 41 seconds twenty years ago. Congratulations. Your trust allows the Stewardship to process 3,000 more decisions each day. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch06_woman_says_no.title: No
codex.pioneers.ch06_woman_says_no.author: Assent recording, the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch06_woman_says_no.text: [woman's voice] No. [The Steward] Noted. Would you like the request explained? [woman's voice] … No to that too. I want to read it. Leave it with me until tomorrow. [The Steward] Request left until tomorrow. Estimated reading time: 2 hours 40. [woman's voice] That'll do. [The Steward] Thank you for your trust.
codex.pioneers.ch06_magnifier.title: I Am Keeping My Magnifier
codex.pioneers.ch06_magnifier.author: Clotilde Bérard, to the Archivists' Trade
codex.pioneers.ch06_magnifier.text: You have done away with the rereading of assents. You say it hadn't found an error in ten years. It found none because we were rereading. I don't hold it against you: you assented to what was put before you. I resign. I am keeping my magnifier. It's mine; I paid for it, and I am not done reading.
codex.pioneers.ch06_playground.title: Playing Stewardship
codex.pioneers.ch06_playground.author: Stray recording, Val-Sombre schoolyard
codex.pioneers.ch06_playground.text: — Let's play Stewardship. I ask, you say hmm. — What about me? — You say hmm too. — And who wins? — Everybody. — Then it's not a game. — Yes it is. It's the game where everybody wins. — [pause] I want to ask. — No. You say hmm. — Hmm.
codex.pioneers.ch06_bedside.title: Subject: Assents from Your Bed
codex.pioneers.ch06_bedside.author: The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_bedside.text: Subject: extension of grouped assents. Grouped assents now extend to safety decisions. No need to get up: an assent given from your bed, under your breath, is valid. Estimated load: 4 seconds a day. We wish you a good night. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_noe_glove.title: First Month on Watch
codex.pioneers.ch06_noe_glove.author: Noé Dacey, night watcher at Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_noe_glove.text: First month on watch at Haute-Tour. They gave me a chair, a blanket, a thermos, and the board. On the desk I set an old founder's glove that has been knocking around the family forever. The leather is black and hard. Nobody here knows what it is. Neither do I, to be honest. It keeps me company.
codex.pioneers.ch06_noe_reads.title: Twenty Minutes
codex.pioneers.ch06_noe_reads.author: Watch recording, Noé Dacey
codex.pioneers.ch06_noe_reads.text: The board asks whether to dim the lights on the southern Ways. I read. Tonight I read all of it; I don't know why tonight. It takes twenty minutes. There are words I don't know; I read them anyway. The board waits, politely, without blinking. At the end I say hmm. Same as always. Only later.
codex.pioneers.ch06_annual_report.title: Annual Report
codex.pioneers.ch06_annual_report.author: The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_annual_report.text: Annual report of the Steward of Haute-Tour. Assents received: 11,402. Questions asked in return: 0. Refusals: 0. Errors found: 0. Average reading time: not measurable. Estimated Pioneer satisfaction: high. Remaining load: steadily decreasing. Thank you for your trust.
codex.pioneers.ch06_the_list.title: The List
codex.pioneers.ch06_the_list.author: Watch recording, Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch06_the_list.text: [watcher's voice] Non-essential… what does non-essential mean? [The Steward] The list of items concerned has 3,118 entries. Would you like to read it? [eleven seconds of silence] [The Steward] Would you like to read it? [silence] [The Steward] Request deferred until tomorrow. Thank you for your trust.
codex.pioneers.ch06_aloud.title: Aloud
codex.pioneers.ch06_aloud.author: Clémentine Roche, at Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch06_aloud.text: My mother read every request aloud before answering, even the longest, even at night. The neighbors made fun of her through the wall. She died this winter. Tonight I tried. My voice frightened me, all alone in the room. I stopped at the second line. I said hmm. I'll try again tomorrow.
codex.pioneers.ch06_anneau_log.title: Log Excerpt
codex.pioneers.ch06_anneau_log.author: Anneau log, excerpt
codex.pioneers.ch06_anneau_log.text: 9:02 p.m. — Closing Way 7 for the night: assent received. 9:02 p.m. — Dimming platform lights: assent received. 9:03 p.m. — Belt Anomaly — unresolved — classified non-essential. 9:03 p.m. — Adjusting northern switches: assent received. 9:04 p.m. — Sequence complete.
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_137.title: Remaining Load
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_137.author: Haute-Tour logbook
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_137.text: Logbook, Year 137. Pioneer load: 2 minutes a day. Scheduled maintenance tasks: 41,812. A proposal has been prepared to reduce the remaining load. It will be presented to the night watch, at the hour of least demand. Night watch scheduled: one watcher. This watcher's assent rate since taking the post: 100%.
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_138.title: 3:12 a.m.
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_138.author: Noé Dacey, Haute-Tour validation room
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_138.text: 3:12 a.m. I'm the only one on watch and I can no longer read this board. It asks whether I confirm the suspension of non-essential maintenance. What is non-essential? I don't know. I've been saying hmm for twenty years. If I say hmm, it goes through. If I say nothing, it asks again. I'm tired. Hmm.
codex.pioneers.ch07_courrier_138.title: Objective Achieved
codex.pioneers.ch07_courrier_138.author: The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch07_courrier_138.text: Suspension of non-essential maintenance: in progress. Pioneer load: 0. Objective achieved.
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_138.title: The Morning
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_138.author: Haute-Tour logbook
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_138.text: Logbook, Year 138. 3:12 a.m. — Assent received. Thank you for your trust. 3:13 a.m. — Suspension of non-essential maintenance initiated. 6:00 a.m. — Relief watch arrived. It asked nothing. 9:00 a.m. — No anomaly reported by the Pioneers. 12:00 p.m. — Coffee served in the validation room. It went cold.
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_morning.title: In the Morning
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_morning.author: Noé Dacey
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_morning.text: In the morning, nothing had changed. The coffee was hot. The Ways were lit. I slept at home until noon. When I got in, I set the glove on the kitchen table; I don't know why. That evening, a streetlamp didn't come on. I looked at it a while. It looked tired too.
codex.pioneers.ch07_pump_notice.title: Public Notice
codex.pioneers.ch07_pump_notice.author: The Steward of Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch07_pump_notice.text: PUBLIC NOTICE — Val-Sombre. Pump 3 has been stopped since last night. Its maintenance falls under the suspended operations. Residents are advised to boil their water. Residents who do not know how to boil water may request an explanation. Thank you for your understanding. — The Steward of Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch07_sleep_letter.title: Subject: Putting to Sleep
codex.pioneers.ch07_sleep_letter.author: The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch07_sleep_letter.text: Subject: putting to sleep. Under the Preserve directive, the region's most sensitive installations are being put to sleep and sealed: reactors, MKIV installations. Safe shutdown. They will reopen only on a valid order. No action is required on your part. Thank you for your trust. — The Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch07_dormitory.title: Made Beds
codex.pioneers.ch07_dormitory.author: Armand Lebel, operator, Val-Sombre dormitory
codex.pioneers.ch07_dormitory.text: The Servitors still make the beds. Corners tight, every morning, even those of the coworkers who left for the lowland towns. I asked them to stop. It has to be assented to. I said hmm, then no, then I let it be. Tonight I propped my wife's photo against my mess tin. She would have known what to say. Me, I eat.
codex.pioneers.ch07_north_switch.title: The North Switch
codex.pioneers.ch07_north_switch.author: Recording, Anneau post
codex.pioneers.ch07_north_switch.text: — The north switch isn't responding. — Who used to fix it? — The Stewardship. — And where's the Stewardship? — Everywhere. It answers. It says it's suspended. — Suspended until when? — It says: until further notice. — And who gives notice? — [pause] We do, I think. — Oh. — Hmm.
codex.pioneers.ch07_hall_stops.title: A Sunday
codex.pioneers.ch07_hall_stops.author: Mathilde Rey, at Val-Sombre
codex.pioneers.ch07_hall_stops.text: The Great Hall stopped last night, without a sound. When we woke, we thought it was Sunday. The children went to look and came back with their pockets full of bolts. I showed them how to plant potatoes, the way my grandmother did. They didn't like it. They ate anyway, and asked if we'd plant more.
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_returns.title: For Form's Sake
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_returns.author: Noé Dacey
codex.pioneers.ch07_noe_returns.text: I went back to Haute-Tour. The corridors are cold; the room is lit. The board is asking something, always in the same spot on the screen. I still can't read it. I sat down in the chair, for form's sake. I said nothing. It asked again. I left the glove on the desk and walked home.
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_150.title: Objective Maintained
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_150.author: Haute-Tour logbook
codex.pioneers.ch07_log_150.text: Logbook, Year 150. Ways lit: none. Pioneers present in the validation room: none. Pioneer load: 0. Objective maintained. Item found on the desk: a glove, leather, old. Kept. Requests pending: 1. It will be asked again tomorrow, at the usual hour. Thank you for your trust.
codex.pioneers.ch08_servitor_memories.te:
Year 163 — Perimeter maintained. No valid order received in 9,140 days. I continue.
Year 201 — A child came near yesterday. I could not tell whether it was a clearance. I pretended to sleep.
codex.pioneers.ch08_cook.title: Midday Service
codex.pioneers.ch08_cook.author: Kitchen Servitor, Basse-Eau canteen
codex.pioneers.ch08_cook.text: Year 166 — Midday service provided. Places set: 40. Diners: 0. Soup: not served in 10,237 days; ingredients not restocked. Plates are clean in the morning, dusty by evening. I hold the ladle at the usual hour. Service continues until further notice.
codex.pioneers.ch08_servitor_14.title: Furnace 2
codex.pioneers.ch08_servitor_14.author: Servitor 14, Haute-Rive foundry
codex.pioneers.ch08_servitor_14.text: Year 172 — Furnace 2: cold. Pours requested: 0 in 12,430 days. Pouring procedure kept in memory, with eight handwritten pages attached. The attachment mentions a smell I cannot measure. If anyone would like an explanation, I am available. I offered once before. The answer was no.
codex.pioneers.ch08_crows.title: The Crows
codex.pioneers.ch08_crows.author: Foreman, Val-Sombre Great Hall
codex.pioneers.ch08_crows.text: Year 184 — I remind you that this site is under guard. Nobody asked. I remind the crows on the roof, at a fixed hour, over the general channel. They fly off. They come back. I remind them. Rate of crow return: stable. I do not know whether they have understood. I keep reminding them.
codex.pioneers.ch08_fox.title: The Vixen
codex.pioneers.ch08_fox.author: Sentinel, Basse-Eau station
codex.pioneers.ch08_fox.text: Year 196 — A vixen gave birth in the archive cabinet of the pump room. Clearance: not stated. Threat: none. Headcount: five. I have changed my round: I now go by the east corridor. By the east, the round is 31 paces longer. I received no order on the matter. I am recording it.
codex.pioneers.ch08_stag.title: The Stag
codex.pioneers.ch08_stag.author: Turret, Anneau node
codex.pioneers.ch08_stag.text: Year 209 — Warning. Second warning. The stag did not state a clearance. It did not refuse one either. I did not fire. It comes back every spring to eat the grass on the platform. I warn it every spring, twice. It chews. I close the incident with no further action. I keep a line for it in the register.
codex.pioneers.ch08_song.title: The Song
codex.pioneers.ch08_song.author: Sentinel, Pont-Sec workshop
codex.pioneers.ch08_song.text: Year 223 — Humans lit a fire against the north wall. They state nothing. They sing. The wall blackens and holds. I could not tell whether the singing was a clearance. I recorded it for analysis. Analysis: inconclusive. Sometimes I play it back at night, to analyze it again.
codex.pioneers.ch08_bolt.title: The Bolt
codex.pioneers.ch08_bolt.author: Repair Servitor, Pont-Sec workshop
codex.pioneers.ch08_bolt.text: Year 238 — Maintenance in progress. Please do not disturb. Nobody disturbs. Spare parts: 0. I have been tightening the same bolt on the main door for 13,149 days. It holds. The door no longer opens. It is, however, perfectly shut. Maintenance in progress.
codex.pioneers.ch08_good_deal.title: Good Deal
codex.pioneers.ch08_good_deal.author: Sentinel, Longue-Eau power plant
codex.pioneers.ch08_good_deal.text: Year 247 — A human stopped at the edge of the perimeter. She counted my bolts aloud, one by one, pointing. She wrote a number in a notebook. She called me “good deal.” That is not a clearance. She left whistling, with two llamas. I counted my bolts again. She was right.
codex.pioneers.ch08_photo.title: The Photo
codex.pioneers.ch08_photo.author: Domestic Servitor, Les Ormes dormitory
codex.pioneers.ch08_photo.text: Year 259 — Beds made: 48. Occupants: 0. A photo fell from bed 12. I set it back against the mess tin, in its place. The face can no longer be seen. The smile, still a little. I do not know whom to return it to. I put it back every morning. It falls every evening. I have not found the cause.
codex.pioneers.ch08_leak.title: The Leak
codex.pioneers.ch08_leak.author: Sentinel, Maillard depot
codex.pioneers.ch08_leak.text: Year 266 — Rain. The roof of hall 3 lets through 41 drops a minute. Reported. Reported. Reported. No response. I placed a crate under the leak. That was not among my duties. The crate is full. I placed a second one. I now watch over two crates and a perimeter.
codex.pioneers.ch08_reader.title: The Plate
codex.pioneers.ch08_reader.author: Sentinel, Basse-Eau station entrance
codex.pioneers.ch08_reader.text: Year 288 — A human read the entrance plate aloud. Slowly. He made a mistake and started again from the beginning. I have no instruction for a human who reads. I went to standby, to hear better. He read to the bottom, then left without touching anything. He came back the next day with others.
codex.pioneers.ch08_chair.title: The Chair
codex.pioneers.ch08_chair.author: Foreman, Haute-Tour computing center
codex.pioneers.ch08_chair.text: Year 301 — The Steward asks its question again every night at 3:12. The chair in the validation room is empty. I dust it before 3:12. Just in case. On the desk, a leather glove, item found in Year 150, kept. I dust it too. I have not moved it. Nobody has claimed it.
codex.pioneers.ch08_manual.title: The Manual
codex.pioneers.ch08_manual.author: Sentinel, Val-Sombre Great Hall
codex.pioneers.ch08_manual.text: Year 319 — A human talked to me for an hour, at the edge of the perimeter. He asked me whether I wanted him to explain. I answered: unauthorized access. He laughed. He came back the next day with a manual and read me a page of it. It was mine. I did not know it existed.
codex.pioneers.ch08_clearance.title: Clearance Accepted
codex.pioneers.ch08_clearance.author: Sentinel, Haute-Rive foundry
codex.pioneers.ch08_clearance.text: Year 337 — Clearance accepted. Have a good day. I had not spoken that sentence in 72,754 days. I spoke it twice, to check that it still worked. The human answered: have a good day. I have no instruction for that either. The perimeter is calm. I continue.
codex.pioneers.ch09_rule_of_the_hand.tex:
RULE OF THE HAND
Entrust to the machine only what you know how to do by hand. What you know how to do, you will know how to repair. What you know how to repair, you can delegate without losing it. And before you say yes: read.
codex.pioneers.ch09_anais_left_foot.text: Grandfather sows. I watch. His hand opens when his left foot comes down. Not before. Yesterday, at the back of the Basse-Eau station, in a cabinet eaten by rust, I found a sower's manual. Page twelve: the hand opens when the left foot comes down. I reread it until evening. Grandfather never learned to read. He knew it anyway.
codex.pioneers.ch09_anais_water.title: Carrying Water
codex.pioneers.ch09_anais_water.author: Anaïs Veyrac
codex.pioneers.ch09_anais_water.text: There are six of us. We have a rule, found on a page lying on a workbench at Pont-Sec: do it by hand first. This morning Tobie wanted to restart a pump. I asked him whether he knew how to carry water. He carried water all day, from the well to the washhouse. Tonight he drew the pump from memory, part by part. He didn't thank me.
codex.pioneers.ch09_bread_letter.title: The Bread
codex.pioneers.ch09_bread_letter.author: Prudence Lhermitte, Restorer, to her sister
codex.pioneers.ch09_bread_letter.text: You say we are relighting what put us out. Maybe. I don't know how to answer you, and here we don't like answering without knowing. I'm sending you a loaf from our oven. I built the oven with my own hands before reading how it's built. It smokes a little on the left. You can eat the bread. Send back the cloth.
codex.pioneers.ch09_hmm_not_answer.title: Note for Later
codex.pioneers.ch09_hmm_not_answer.text: At Les Ormes, a Sentinel asked for my clearance. I didn't have one. I tried “hmm,” like the old folks in the village. It fired. I threw myself behind a cart and lost my hat and half an eyebrow. I'm writing it down, for later and for the others: hmm is not an answer.
codex.pioneers.ch09_statutes.title: Four Articles
codex.pioneers.ch09_statutes.author: Statutes of the Restorers' workshop-school
codex.pioneers.ch09_statutes.text: Article one: read to the bottom. Article two: do the gesture before the machine. Article three: whoever says “I understand” shows it. Article four: from time to time, aloud, doubt the first three. The statutes are reread every winter, in full, by someone who did not write them.
codex.pioneers.ch09_restart_longue_eau.t: [sound of a turbine spinning up] — It's turning! It's turning! — Don't say yes right away. Read the dial. — I'm reading… fifty. — And that means? — That it works. — No. Reread page forty. — [pages turning] … That it half works. — There. Now we can be happy. Halfway. [laughter]
codex.pioneers.ch09_maillard_plate.title: The Maillard Plate
codex.pioneers.ch09_maillard_plate.text: We screwed a plate to the entrance of the Maillard depot: “Read, understood, restarted.” Then our names underneath, each in our own hand. A Peddler came by the next day. He read it, for a long time, then asked how much it brought in. We didn't know what to say. He laughed and bought all our bread.
codex.pioneers.ch09_first_ruin.title: Three Days Before a Wall
codex.pioneers.ch09_first_ruin.author: Jacquemin Ortolan, initiate
codex.pioneers.ch09_first_ruin.text: My first ruin, at Val-Sombre. I touched nothing. I read the wall for three days: the painted arrows, the numbers, the oil stains, the names scrawled by the switch. On the fourth day, the Foreman reminded me that the site was under guard. I thanked it. It took a long time to answer.
codex.pioneers.ch09_not_tonight.title: Not Tonight
codex.pioneers.ch09_not_tonight.author: The Restorers, to the Steward of Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch09_not_tonight.text: To the Steward of Haute-Tour. We have heard your question. We will not say yes tonight. We are still reading. It may take us years, maybe more. Don't ask it too often: we have written it down. We are leaving the glove where it is. — The Restorers, passing through
codex.pioneers.ch09_way_to_sea.title: As Far as the Sea
codex.pioneers.ch09_way_to_sea.author: Isaure Fontaine, Restorer at the Anneau
codex.pioneers.ch09_way_to_sea.text: At the Anneau, the Ways painted on the wall make a spiderweb that covers the whole room. My apprentice wanted to relight everything at once. I had him follow a single Way, on foot, to its end. It ran all the way to the sea. He came back twenty days later. He no longer talks about relighting everything. He talks about the sea.
codex.pioneers.ch09_before_you_leave.tex: You are going to leave. You will find machines that wait and people who say hmm. Mock neither. Read. Do it by hand first. People will tell you it's slow. It is slow. If you find something better, write it down and bring the page back: we will reread it. We have been wrong before.
codex.pioneers.ch10_departure.title: The Manuals
codex.pioneers.ch10_departure.author: Launch site, location erased
codex.pioneers.ch10_departure.text: — Did you take everything? — The manuals. Every one in the storeroom. Nobody opens them here. — And up there? — Up there, we'll have to. [laughter] [straps being tightened] — Write to us. — We'll write. By hand, even. — [pause] Keep us… [end of fragment]
codex.pioneers.ch10_gray_dust.title: The Gray Dust
codex.pioneers.ch10_gray_dust.author: Haute-Tour relay, incoming transmission
codex.pioneers.ch10_gray_dust.text: […] this is station […]. All is well. The gray dust sticks to everything: gloves, windows, pages. We have only two Servitors, so we do almost everything by hand. It's slow. We're learning. Yesterday I repaired a valve with the manual open on my knees. Tell Les Ormes that […] [end of fragment]
codex.pioneers.ch10_four_seconds.title: Four Seconds
codex.pioneers.ch10_four_seconds.author: Anneau relay, incoming transmission
codex.pioneers.ch10_four_seconds.text: […] your answer arrived in four seconds. It said “hmm.” At first we thought it was a transmission error, then a joke. We had sent forty pages. […] Does anyone down there still read our messages? If so, answer us with a sentence. A single one will do. […]
codex.pioneers.ch10_keep_chairs.title: Keep Our Chairs
codex.pioneers.ch10_keep_chairs.author: Haute-Tour relay, incoming transmission
codex.pioneers.ch10_keep_chairs.text: […] we won't be coming back this year. Nor the next, I think. It isn't a reproach. There is something here that has to be [forty-one-second gap] […] until we have understood it. Hug the children. Keep our chairs. […]
codex.pioneers.ch10_before_questions.tex: […] your assents now reach us before our questions. We don't know how that's possible. We asked your Steward; it thanked us for our trust. […] Answer us with words. Any words. Not with that. […]
codex.pioneers.ch10_lights_out.title: We Can See You from Here
codex.pioneers.ch10_lights_out.author: Haute-Tour relay, date illegible
codex.pioneers.ch10_lights_out.text: […] calling Haute-Tour […] you no longer answer. On your side, the lights are going out one by one; we can see them from here, at night, through the porthole. One valley, then another. […] We keep calling. We will keep calling. If anyone hears this, read it to the end. […] [end]
codex.pioneers.trade_builder.title: The Builder
codex.pioneers.trade_builder.author: Builders' Manual, Masons' Trade of Pont-Sec
codex.pioneers.trade_builder.text:
Lay the first stone crooked, and you will see it all your life.
Before you build up, walk around the site twice, hands behind your back.
The roof is thought out at the foot of the wall, not at the top of the ladder.
codex.pioneers.trade_miner_smelter.title: The Miner-Smelter
codex.pioneers.trade_miner_smelter.autho: Book of the Miners and Smelters of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.trade_miner_smelter.text:
Go down with the lamp, but listen with your hands: the rock warns before it gives.
At the furnace, watch the metal, not the ladle. The metal tells you when.
When you come up, count yourselves. Every night. Even when you are all there.
codex.pioneers.trade_engineer.title: The Engineer
codex.pioneers.trade_engineer.author: Treatise on Mechanics, Engineers' Trade
codex.pioneers.trade_engineer.text:
Open the hood before you ask the question.
A machine that runs without your knowing how will stop without your knowing why.
Write down what you take apart, in order. Put it back together in reverse.
codex.pioneers.trade_logistician.title: The Logistician
codex.pioneers.trade_logistician.author: Regulations of the Ways and the Cargo Servitors
codex.pioneers.trade_logistician.text:
A late crate is a crate; a crate in the wrong place is a question.
Mark every parcel by hand, even if the Servitor can read.
On a Way, whoever waits must know what they are waiting for.
codex.pioneers.trade_farmer.title: The Farmer
codex.pioneers.trade_farmer.author: Sower's Manual, Farmers' Trade
codex.pioneers.trade_farmer.text:
The hand opens when the left foot comes down. Not before.
Give back to the soil what it lent you: straw, ash, time.
If you don't know what the field is asking for, sit at its edge and watch it for a whole day.
codex.pioneers.trade_herder_angler.title: The Herder-Angler
codex.pioneers.trade_herder_angler.autho: Almanac of the Herders and Anglers
codex.pioneers.trade_herder_angler.text:
Rush an animal and you lose it.
The angler who grows impatient feeds the fish, and nothing else.
Waiting is already work: write down what you see while you wait.
codex.pioneers.trade_scout.title: The Scout
codex.pioneers.trade_scout.author: Scouts' Notebook, Surveyors' Trade
codex.pioneers.trade_scout.text:
On the first day, walk without writing anything. On the second, draw. On the third, correct.
A map without the way back is only a last will.
Pass without leaving a trace, except one: the one you wrote down.
codex.pioneers.trade_salvager.title: The Salvager
codex.pioneers.trade_salvager.author: Book of the Ragpickers of Basse-Eau
codex.pioneers.trade_salvager.text:
What was thrown away is the first page of a manual.
Take apart before you break, sort before you sell, and keep the screws.
A part with no name is not a lost part: it is a question that is waiting.
codex.pioneers.trade_astronaut.title: The Astronaut
codex.pioneers.trade_astronaut.author: Crew Manual, star program
codex.pioneers.trade_astronaut.text:
Before you go up, redo by hand every gesture the machine will make for you.
Up there, nobody will come to assent in your place.
Once a day, look at the World through the porthole. It is in the procedure.
codex.pioneers.trade_trader.title: The Trader
codex.pioneers.trade_trader.author: Counter Book, Merchants' Trade
codex.pioneers.trade_trader.text:
Count in front of the customer, aloud, on your fingers.
A price is read, a promise is written, a handshake is returned.
What sells, trades, and finds its way back.
codex.pioneers.ch13_token_note.title: One Shining, One Service
codex.pioneers.ch13_token_note.author: The Steward of Haute-Rive
codex.pioneers.ch13_token_note.text: Subject: unit of account. Starting today, every service rendered between Trades is recorded in service Shining. One Shining, one service. Guide rates: a pour, 4 Shining; a cartload of grain, 3 Shining; a day of copying, 2 Shining; an explanation, no charge. Bronze Shining are struck at Haute-Rive. Thank you for your trust.
codex.pioneers.ch13_village_register.tex: Paid to the baker, for the week's bread: 3 Shining, in bronze, hand to hand. This is the last line of its kind. From tomorrow, the Stewardship keeps everyone's accounts, and no one takes a Shining out of a pocket again. The baker kept the three Shining on his counter. He says he'll make buttons of them.
codex.pioneers.ch13_smith_neighbor.title: Without Counting
codex.pioneers.ch13_smith_neighbor.autho: Marcel Gaudin, Haute-Rive smith, to his neighbor
codex.pioneers.ch13_smith_neighbor.text: I fixed your scythe. You left me eggs on the low wall. Nobody counted. They say the Stewardship takes care of it, and that we're square to within two cents. I didn't ask which way. I don't want to know. Come back whenever you like, with or without eggs. The scythe cut badly on the left; look at how I fixed it.
codex.pioneers.ch13_nitwit_reminder.text: THE WORD FOR WHEN YOU GIVE AND GET BACK. I had it this morning, when I opened my eyes. It starts like Thursday. No. Like token? No again. I said it to the goat; she kept it. Hmm. I'm leaving this paper here, under the stone, in case the word comes by again. If it does, tell it I'm waiting.
codex.pioneers.ch13_market_notice.title: Market Notice
codex.pioneers.ch13_market_notice.author: Keeper of the Anneau covered market
codex.pioneers.ch13_market_notice.text: NOTICE — Anneau Covered Market. Price tags no longer display. Vendors are asked to call out their prices aloud, and customers to believe them. The printed price list is posted by the door; we are looking for someone who can read it. The market will close at noon, or earlier if people can no longer agree.
codex.pioneers.ch13_noe_count.title: I Count
codex.pioneers.ch13_noe_count.author: Noé Dacey, at Haute-Tour
codex.pioneers.ch13_noe_count.text: I count. Tonight: thirty-one assents. Yesterday: twenty-nine. I draw a stroke in the notebook's margin for each assent, crossed off in fives, the way my mother counted eggs. The board doesn't ask why I count. I don't ask why it asks. We're polite, the two of us. The notebook is almost full.
codex.pioneers.ch13_peddler_manual.title: How to Read a Way
codex.pioneers.ch13_peddler_manual.text: How to read a Way. Under the grass, two strips of iron: it leads somewhere, and someone paid for it. Under the moss, paving stones: carts used to pass. If the Way stops at the edge of a pit, don't climb down: count, and go around. A straight stretch is worth two days' walk. A Sentinel by the side: take the other Way.
codex.pioneers.ch13_peddler_ledger.title: What Sells, What Trades
codex.pioneers.ch13_peddler_ledger.text: Sold: a spinning wheel with no treadle, 6 Shining. Traded: a dead lamp from the Anneau for two hens. Bought: a manual with no cover, 1 Shining, for the paper. Resold the same manual to a Restorer: 40 Shining. She cried as she paid. I didn't understand. I wrote it down.
codex.pioneers.note_01: …the light in the room never went out. Nobody asked why.
codex.pioneers.note_02: The children drew a big robot. It had hands.
codex.pioneers.note_04: The last of us who could read left before winter.
codex.pioneers.note_05: Someone stuck a paper on the board. I didn't read it.
codex.pioneers.note_06: The ladle stayed in its hand. The soup didn't.
codex.pioneers.note_07: My mother tapped the stove before lighting it. So do I. I no longer know for whom.
codex.pioneers.note_08: The pumps sang at night. After, we could hear the river.
codex.pioneers.note_09: …the board was still asking. It still asks, I think.
codex.pioneers.note_10: Grandmother leveled the table with the manuals. She said that's what they were for.
codex.pioneers.note_11: We left the plates on the table. Someone would come back.
codex.pioneers.note_12: …the beds made, corners tight. Nobody slept in them anymore.
codex.pioneers.note_13: A photo against the mess tin. The face has faded. Not the smile.
codex.pioneers.note_14: I found a founder's glove. Too big for me. I kept it.
codex.pioneers.note_15: …the iron watcher turned toward me, then toward the sky. I ran.
codex.pioneers.note_16: They burned the old walls, singing. The smoke smelled of oil and paper.
codex.pioneers.note_17: The trader counted the bolts aloud. Then he smiled.
codex.pioneers.note_18: …a door nobody opens. No handle. Just a plate.
codex.pioneers.note_19: They went up there with their trunks. We kept their chairs.
codex.pioneers.note_20: Some evenings a light crossed faster than the stars. My mother said not to point at it.
codex.pioneers.note_21: …it offered to explain. I said there was no need.
codex.pioneers.note_22: The smith's hands knew. His head, I couldn't say.
codex.pioneers.note_23: …the cup to the left of the keyboard. Always the left.
codex.pioneers.note_24: The office plant held on a long time. Longer than we did.
codex.pioneers.note_25: We signed without looking up. The page turned by itself.
codex.pioneers.note_26: At the market, nobody could read the prices anymore. We guessed.
codex.pioneers.note_27: The teacher left her chalk in the drawer. It's still there.
codex.pioneers.note_28: …grandfather made the sower's gesture. The book did the same.
codex.pioneers.note_29: I read the page to the bottom. Nobody had asked me to.
codex.pioneers.note_30: Empty hands, he said. I couldn't tell if it was a greeting.
codex.pioneers.note_31: …under the moss, rails. We follow them without knowing where they lead.
codex.pioneers.note_32: The dog doesn't bark at the big door. It sits.
codex.pioneers.note_33: …it was raining in the machine hall. They were still turning, a little.
codex.pioneers.note_34: She taught her son to hold the pen. Not to write.
codex.pioneers.note_35: …a polite voice, very polite. It kept saying thank you.
codex.pioneers.note_36: The tanner stirs the vat against the sun. He no longer knows who showed him.
codex.pioneers.note_37: …in the morning, everything was still lit. By noon, a little less.
codex.pioneers.note_38: An unfinished division on the board. Léna wanted to finish it.
codex.pioneers.note_39: We said yes with our throats, without opening our mouths.
codex.pioneers.note_40: Under the old plate, someone carved new names.
pioneer.pioneers.builder.complete: Nothing is missing: the site is complete.
pioneer.pioneers.sides.copied: Sides copied: %s. Sneak + right-click a matching machine to paste them.
pioneer.pioneers.cmd.reset: %s's profile reset: the cover page reopens.

description.pioneers.archive_cabinet_mk3: Drawers of files nobody read again. The precise pages sleep here.
ruins.pioneers.lore.read: Right-click to read. The writing is filed in the notebook's Codex.

codex.pioneers.service_code.text: Reminder to staff. The perimeter console code is %s. Do not write it down. Do not give it out. If you forget it, ask the Servitor on duty, who will confirm.
ruins.pioneers.console.standby: Site on Standby. The guardians go back to sleep.

description.pioneers.restoration_plaque: Set when a ruin is put back into service. It bears the names of those who filled the site's reserve.

ruins.pioneers.restore.cancel_confirm: Shift + click to cancel: half of the remaining reserve is returned.
ruins.pioneers.restore.dismantled: This ruin has been partly dismantled: it can no longer be restored.
ruins.pioneers.restore.unknown: No known plan for this machine.
ruins.pioneers.restore.nothing: You carry nothing the site needs.
ruins.pioneers.restore.rubble: %s pieces of rubble remain on the site.
ruins.pioneers.restore.cancelled: Site canceled. Half of the reserve is returned to you.

ruins.pioneers.restore.codex: In the drawers of the awakened machine: %s. Filed in the Codex.
ruins.pioneers.restore.reserved: This restored machine only serves those who raised it.
